bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity concentration - 100% of turnover from real estate — BRSR Section A reports Real Estate (including facility management, with owned or leased assets) as the sole business activity at 100% of turnover, and Real Estate Development as the sole product/service at 100% of turnover. There is no second earnings stream to cushion a downturn in the property cycle.
- Geographic concentration in Delhi NCR — The Company states it "has strategically chosen to focus currently on developing multiple asset classes in Delhi NCR", with exports not applicable and registered/corporate offices only in Noida (UP), Okhla (New Delhi) and Gurugram (Haryana). Regulatory, approval, infrastructure or demand shocks specific to the NCR micro-markets hit the entire portfolio at once.
- Environmental compliance — Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table: "Non-compliance with environmental regulations can result in penalties, legal consequences, and reputational harm", with negative financial implications of potential fines, legal costs and reputational damage. Mitigation is an environmental management system, adherence to regulations, monitoring and reporting, and a zero-tolerance policy on non-compliance.
- Unpredictable climate patterns — Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material issues table, citing increasing climate-related events (floods, heatwaves, thunderstorms, smog situations) - relevant for a business whose construction schedules, site safety and operating assets are exposed to weather and air-quality disruption.
- Execution and approval dependency on new land/SPV acquisitions — The Board's Report qualifies the projected booking value of more than Rs 3,000 crore from the Base Buildwell (Sector 59, Gurugram) acquisition as "subject to project execution timelines, requisite approvals and market conditions", making a material part of the growth pipeline contingent on regulatory clearance and market absorption.
- Rising customer complaint volume — BRSR transparency disclosures record 1,662 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 against 914 in FY 2024-25 (classified as Commercial and Residential, none related to delivery of essential services), all closed with none pending. The near-doubling alongside portfolio scale-up is a service-quality and brand watch-item; Factech Software has been implemented across all commercial operational sites.
- Employee attrition, particularly among women — Permanent employee turnover was 16% in FY 2025-26 (14% male, 25% female) versus 15% in FY 2024-25 and 18% in FY 2023-24. With women at only 17% of the workforce, the materially higher female attrition rate works against the stated diversity agenda and against retention of a workforce being scaled to support the project pipeline.
- Legacy shareholder/legal matter at a subsidiary — A BRSR grievance note records a complaint pertaining to "a legacy matter involving a former shareholder of Pharmax Corporation Limited, a Subsidiary of the Company" - a residual claim carried in through an acquired SPV, illustrating inherited-liability exposure in the acquisition-led growth model.
- Partial ownership of material operating subsidiaries — Several material project SPVs are not wholly owned - Max Towers Private Limited, Max Square Limited, Pharmax Corporation Limited and Acreage Builders Private Limited are each 51%-held and Max Estates Noida Private Limited is 60%-held - so a meaningful share of asset-level economics accrues to non-controlling interests and requires partner alignment.
- No external assurance on the BRSR/sustainability disclosures — BRSR Section A items 14 and 15 record the name of assurance provider and type of assurance obtained as "Not Applicable", so the ESG data underpinning the sustainability narrative is unassured.

outlook.body:
- "Max Estates 3.0" journey - transition from the execution phase to execution at scale, with FY26 described as delivering on the promises made at the launch of that journey
- Focused Delhi-NCR strategy: build a diversified platform across residential, commercial and mixed-use assets concentrated in Gurugram and Noida, with access to prime development opportunities across high-growth corridors
- Premium-to-ultra-premium residential positioning, evidenced by average price realisation rising from Rs 18,410 per sq. ft. in FY24 to Rs 23,789 per sq. ft. in FY26 (13% CAGR)
- Keep residential execution completely debt-free by funding construction through internal accruals, supported by a disciplined payment structure yielding steady annual collections of around 20-25% of total sales value
- Build a maturing commercial annuity platform under the WorkWell philosophy as a structural counterbalance to residential cash flows
- Pre-lease commercial assets well ahead of completion at a premium to micro-market rates, converting the Max Estates address into rental premium
- Agile product recalibration in response to market signals - e.g. repositioning Estate 105 to a revised mix of residential and serviced apartments to double GDV potential
- Capital-efficient business development anchored by the strategic partnership with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL), including project-level co-investment to keep projects fully capitalised
- Acquire and revive stalled/underdeveloped land and projects through SPV acquisitions (BPPL/Delhi One revival as Max One; Sector 59 development rights)
- Institutionalise scale through SOPs across 13 critical verticals of the real estate value chain, reviewed through internal audits
- Build an end-to-end digital execution ecosystem mapped to the value chain (SAP ERP, Salesforce, Ozonetel, Reloy; ZOHO HRMS, Teamlease, Klimb, Q-Cop, SharePoint DMS, Slack)
- Grow and diversify the talent base to support the pipeline, including a stated target of 30% women representation
- Sustainability and ESG as a design principle - top-tier LEED, WELL and IGBC Platinum certifications, GRESB participation, Scope 1 and 2 net-zero progress and Scope 3 baselining
- Community building as a leasing/brand differentiator via the Pulse tenant-engagement platform and social impact partnerships such as the Latika Centre for Inclusion
- The Company frames capital allocation as one of three pillars of its group governance framework: "Capital Management Discipline: We prioritize prudent capital management practices to ensure the responsible allocation of resources and sustainable growth", alongside Performance Management Excellence and Stakeholder Value Creation. Boards are explicitly charged with strategy formulation, financial monitoring through rigorous oversight mechanisms, risk management and succession planning, with material matters reviewed by Board sub-committees comprising a balanced mix of Non-Executive and Independent Directors under detailed charters. No dividend policy, payout intent or buyback is stated in the routed sections, and Form AOC-1 records "NA" for proposed dividend across all subsidiaries. Part B of Form AOC-1 is not applicable as the Company has no associates or joint ventures.
- Energy Efficiency & Emissions identified as a material opportunity - improve energy efficiency and benchmark performance with market trends, with expected positive implications from reduced energy costs and operational savings
- Building Material Efficiency pursued through a 4R strategy - Reduce, Reuse, Recycle & Replenish - and the search for sustainable substitutes, targeting cost savings, reduced waste and reduced embodied carbon
- Water Efficiency treated as material because water availability is critical to all stages of real estate development; implementing water efficiency measures to reduce water costs and demonstrate environmental stewardship
- Environmental compliance managed through an environmental management system, adherence to regulations, monitoring and reporting on compliance, and a zero-tolerance policy on non-compliance
- Climate resilience recognised as a material risk given increasing climate-related events (floods, heatwaves, thunderstorms, smog situations)
- 95% employee coverage achieved under ESG-related training initiatives
- Governance, ethics and sustainability policies extended across Max Estates and all its subsidiaries to ensure a consistent approach to responsible business conduct
- Board gender diversity at 33% women directors; women at 17% of the permanent workforce (83% male), with a strengthened DEI agenda focused on multiculturalism, gender diversity and equal opportunity, including gender diversity across project execution teams
- WorkWell philosophy extended across project sites covering safety, welfare, ergonomics, mental well-being and employee amenities for employees and workforce partners
- Disability inclusion through engagement of The Maalish Co., an inclusive social enterprise creating livelihood opportunities for blind, visually impaired and deaf professionals who provide regular workplace wellness sessions at Max Towers
- CSR under Section 135 applicable in FY26; INR 100 lakh contributed to Max India Foundation on a standalone basis and INR 16.25 lakh through subsidiaries, for a total of INR 116.25 lakh on a consolidated basis
- Stakeholder-specific grievance redressal channels maintained for communities, investors and shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, including a Vigil Mechanism and Whistle Blower framework for employees and value chain partners
- Nil sexual harassment complaints received, disposed of or pending during FY26 under the POSH policy, with the Internal Committee duly constituted
- Compensation structures revised in line with Labour Code requirements to strengthen statutory compliance
- BRSR reported on a consolidated boundary for FY 2025-26, with no assurance provider appointed and no assurance obtained
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Max Estates' expansion is land- and project-led rather than plant-led, concentrated in Delhi-NCR (Noida and Gurugram) across commercial, residential and mixed-use asset classes, executed through dedicated project SPVs. On the commercial side, two large assets are under design and development: Max District, Sector 65 on Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram - a ~4-acre parcel with ~0.9 mn sq. ft. of office area and 0.1 mn sq. ft. of retail within a 1.6 million sq. ft. leasable-area development, LEED Platinum and WiredScore Platinum pre-certified, progressing on track for occupancy certificates in two phases (Phase 1 in Q2 FY28 and Phase 2 in Q3 FY29), with 200,000 sq. ft. already pre-leased at a 35%+ premium to the micro-market locking in over Rs 270 crore of gross rentals over a nine-year term two-and-a-half years before completion; and Max Square Two, Sector 129 Noida - a 7.35-acre parcel with ~1.6 mn sq. ft. leasable area (project stated at 1 million sq. ft. leasable), IGBC Platinum pre-certified with WELL certification under process, on track for its occupation certificate by Q2 FY28, with ~86,000 sq. ft. pre-leased at a ~25% premium securing over Rs 95 crore of gross rentals. Together with the delivered assets (Max House Phases I and II, Max Towers, Max Square, all at 100% occupancy), the commercial portfolio - delivered, under-construction and acquisition-stage - is positioned to reach annuity rental income potential exceeding Rs 700 crore on a 100% basis over the next five years. On the residential side the pipeline GDV exceeds Rs 17,200 crore: Estate 361 (18 acres, ~4 mn sq. ft. saleable, Rs 9,000 crore overall potential) launched Phase 1 in Q3 FY26 at ~Rs 2,500 crore GDV and added The Terraces precinct in May 2026 with an incremental Rs 1,200 crore of GDV; Estate 105, Sector 105 Noida (~10 acres, ~2.6 mn sq. ft. potential) was launched in March 2026 at ~Rs 3,000 crore initial GDV and repositioned to a residential plus serviced-apartment mix that doubled GDV potential to ~Rs 6,000 crore, with Phase 2 planned for FY27; and Sector 59, Golf Course Extension Road Gurugram (7.25 acres, ~1.3 mn sq. ft. potential, GDV potential Rs 3,900+ crore) is targeted for launch in Q4 FY27. Inorganic footprint additions during FY26 were made through SPV acquisitions - Boulevard Projects Private Limited (acquired 23 April 2025, enabling the revival of the stalled "Delhi One" development in Sector 16B Noida as Max One after RERA clearances) and Base Buildwell Private Limited (acquired 26 December 2025, the Sector 59 Gurugram land parcel, total transaction outlay ~Rs 534.32 crore covering share capital, security deposit, purchase of Transferable Development Rights and related approvals) - alongside incorporation of two new wholly-owned subsidiaries, Max Estates Noida Two Limited (1 September 2025) and Max Estates Developers Limited (30 January 2026). Capacity to execute is being built out on the organisational side too: the workforce expanded to 309 permanent employees with 129 onboarded across 20 functions in FY26 (about 10x headcount growth over the last few years), SOPs institutionalised across 13 critical verticals of the value chain, and a digital ecosystem (SAP, Salesforce, Ozonetel, Reloy and HR platforms) deployed to support scale. Funding for the Noida build-out was secured through a Rs 584 crore Compulsory Convertible Debenture co-investment with New York Life Insurance Company (NYL Rs 293 crore, Max Estates Rs 291 crore), with FY26 concluded at negligible net debt and residential execution funded through internal accruals.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's domestic economy remained stable and resilient with FY26 real GDP growth estimated at 7.4%, the fastest-growing major economy for the fourth consecutive year, supported by steady consumption, historically low inflation and robust investment - against a fragile global environment of geopolitical tensions and trade fragmentation
- India's real estate market continued to consolidate: rising household incomes, infrastructure development and premiumisation supported demand even as participation by smaller developers in new launches declined
- New supply is becoming increasingly concentrated among branded, diversified developers with prudent balance sheets; relatively low inventory overhang gives them headroom to sustain launches, accelerate asset churn and capture market share
- Residential sales entered a more calibrated phase, but demand for premium and luxury housing remained resilient across major cities, supported by shifting lifestyle preferences and strong end-user demand
- Delhi-NCR continued to stand out as one of India's most dynamic real estate markets with strong traction across premium residential and commercial assets, reinforcing the relevance of the focused NCR strategy
- Residential collections follow a disciplined payment structure delivering steady annual collections of around 20-25% of total sales value, giving predictable cash flow to fund construction from internal accruals
- Commercial annuity income trajectory is maturing rapidly across delivered, under-construction and acquisition-stage assets, providing a long-dated institutional income stream
- Grade A workspace demand keeps operational commercial assets at 100% occupancy, and forward leasing is being locked in at a premium to prevailing micro-market rates
- Solar power implementation at Max Square cuts electricity costs by 20% to 25% alongside an annual emission reduction of 6,000 tonnes - an operating cost lever
- Scale-up of headcount (10x growth over the last few years; 129 professionals onboarded in FY26 with focused hiring in the residential vertical) to support upcoming high-value launches
- Cumulative residential presales to date of Rs 12,500 crore
- Future pipeline with a Gross Development Value exceeding Rs 17,200 crore
- FY26 record presales of Rs 5,305 crore - second consecutive year of surpassing the Rs 5,000 crore milestone; FY26 collections up 61% Y-o-Y to Rs 1,578 crore
- Estate 361: Rs 1,704 crore of presales with over 68% of Phase 1-launched inventory (GDV Rs 2,500 crore) cleared; The Terraces precinct introduced in May 2026 adds Rs 1,200 crore of GDV to a master project with overall potential of Rs 9,000 crore
- Estate 105: launched March 2026 with an initial GDV of ~Rs 3,000 crore and achieved ~Rs 1,783 crore of presales within ten days; repositioning has doubled GDV potential to ~Rs 6,000 crore ahead of a planned Phase 2 launch in FY27
- Max One (revival of the stalled "Delhi One" development, Sector 16B Noida): contributed ~Rs 1,415 crore to FY26 presales, including Rs 1,221 crore recognised post receipt of RERA that had been booked by the erstwhile developer
- Estate 360: cumulative presales booking value of Rs 4,831 crore alongside collections of Rs 1,636 crore, with construction progressing as planned
- Sector 59, Golf Course Extension Road, Gurugram: development rights secured with GDV potential of Rs 3,900+ crore, launch targeted for Q4 FY27
- Commercial operating assets (Max Towers, Max House Phases I & II, Max Square) at 100% occupancy generating aggregate annual rentals of Rs 158 crore
- Max District pre-leasing agreement locking in over Rs 270 crore of gross rentals over a nine-year term, secured two-and-a-half years before scheduled completion at a 35% premium to micro-market rates
- Max Square Two: ~86,000 sq. ft. pre-leased securing over Rs 95 crore in gross rentals, with a robust leasing pipeline maintained across both flagship assets
- Commercial portfolio annuity rental income potential exceeding Rs 700 crore on a 100% basis over the next five years

The company sits on a massive locked-in revenue pipeline (INR 12,500 cr sold but unrecognized) and a near-net-zero debt position, positioning it to scale annuity income to INR 700 cr over 5 years despite near-term geopolitical caution.

risks.note: BRSR Section A reports Real Estate (including facility management, with owned or leased assets) as the sole business activity at 100% of turnover, and Real Estate Development as the sole product/service at 100% of turnover. There is no second earnings stream to cushion a downturn in the property cycle.
risks.risk: Single-activity concentration - 100% of turnover from real estate

risks.note: The Company states it "has strategically chosen to focus currently on developing multiple asset classes in Delhi NCR", with exports not applicable and registered/corporate offices only in Noida (UP), Okhla (New Delhi) and Gurugram (Haryana). Regulatory, approval, infrastructure or demand shocks specific to the NCR micro-markets hit the entire portfolio at once.

Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table: "Non-compliance with environmental regulations can result in penalties, legal consequences, and reputational harm", with negative financial implications of potential fines, legal costs and reputational damage. Mitigation is an environmental management system, adherence to regulations, monitoring and reporting, and a zero-tolerance policy on non-compliance.

Flagged as a Risk in the BRSR material issues table, citing increasing climate-related events (floods, heatwaves, thunderstorms, smog situations) - relevant for a business whose construction schedules, site safety and operating assets are exposed to weather and air-quality disruption.

The Board's Report qualifies the projected booking value of more than Rs 3,000 crore from the Base Buildwell (Sector 59, Gurugram) acquisition as "subject to project execution timelines, requisite approvals and market conditions", making a material part of the growth pipeline contingent on regulatory clearance and market absorption.
risks.risk: Execution and approval dependency on new land/SPV acquisitions

risks.note: BRSR transparency disclosures record 1,662 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 against 914 in FY 2024-25 (classified as Commercial and Residential, none related to delivery of essential services), all closed with none pending. The near-doubling alongside portfolio scale-up is a service-quality and brand watch-item; Factech Software has been implemented across all commercial operational sites.

Permanent employee turnover was 16% in FY 2025-26 (14% male, 25% female) versus 15% in FY 2024-25 and 18% in FY 2023-24. With women at only 17% of the workforce, the materially higher female attrition rate works against the stated diversity agenda and against retention of a workforce being scaled to support the project pipeline.

A BRSR grievance note records a complaint pertaining to "a legacy matter involving a former shareholder of Pharmax Corporation Limited, a Subsidiary of the Company" - a residual claim carried in through an acquired SPV, illustrating inherited-liability exposure in the acquisition-led growth model.
risks.risk: Legacy shareholder/legal matter at a subsidiary
